check_service_status.description: Check whether the CSS Colors API is answering, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being reachable but not serving colours is reported separately from being down.

mock_response.message: The CSS Colors API is up and answering.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

message.description: What was found, in one sentence.

online.description: True when the service answered with a colour.

reachable.description: True when the service answered at all, even with an error.

response_time_ms.description: How long it took to answer, in milliseconds; empty if it did not answer.

status_code.description: The HTTP status it answered with; empty if it did not answer.

find_nearest_color.description: Find the named CSS colour closest to any colour value: a hex such as #1E90FE, a short hex such as #19F, or channels such as rgb(30, 144, 254). The service has no lookup by value, so the table is read once and every colour measured against the value, weighted the way the eye weights the channels. An exact match is reported as one, names that share the value (Aqua and Cyan, Gray and Grey) come back as aliases, and the next nearest colours are listed with their distances so a step that wants a choice has one.

find_nearest_color.name: find_nearest_color

parameters.name: color

parameters.name: candidate_count

group.description: The group the service files it under, such as Blue or Gray.

hsl.description: The colour as CSS hsl(), such as hsl(210, 100%, 56%).

rgb.description: The colour as CSS rgb(), such as rgb(30, 144, 255).

theme.description: light or dark: the service's call on whether black text (light) or white text (dark) reads on the colour as a background.

Pick a name from the list or type one from an earlier step: case, spaces and hyphens do not matter, so dodger blue finds DodgerBlue. An unknown name is reported as such, with a pointer to the search.

get_random_color.description: Pick one CSS colour at random, from the whole table or from one group or theme, for a placeholder, a swatch of the day or a themed post. Give a seed to get the same colour every time for that seed: seed with the date and a daily post that retries, or that two people run an hour apart, picks the same colour, while tomorrow picks a different one.

search_colors.description: Find the CSS colours whose name contains a word, best match first: a name that is the word, then names that start with it, then names that merely contain it, so a search for blue leads with Blue and BlueViolet before AliceBlue. Spaces and case are ignored, so sky blue finds SkyBlue. The service has no search of its own, so the table is read once and matched here, and the total number of matches is always reported.

description: Look up the 148 named CSS colours from the CSS Colors API, the free keyless reference to the colour names every browser understands. Get a colour's hex, rgb() and hsl() forms by name, list a group such as the blues or the greys, list the light or the dark ones so text stays readable, search the names for a word, find the named colour nearest to any hex so a brand value gets a name, or pick one at random for a swatch of the day.
